name: round-2
note: Second round, on a new baseline. Round one (tempo-on-off) ended with one change that held up on the ladder: holding the frostburst for the opening against bots rated 2250 and up (+15 points at 2.1 standard errors there, -11 under 2250). The scouts' default playbook becomes that rating-based playbook (field-marshal/playbooks/default.json written by tools/flagship-playbook.py --out, same as the flagship's), and control is that default. The three arms are questions round one left open because their games were played before the connection fix or were cut short: frost-escape (dash out of a burst thrown at us; +5 points after 51 games), no-tempo (is the tempo evaluation at the leaves worth having; 13 clean games), plan-8 (eight ticks of our own lines against an opponent model; no clean games). Each arm is laid over the per-opponent default, so it changes one thing against every opponent. Every opponent, balanced by opponent, map and seat. Read each arm against control and the plain default games over the same hours, by opponent rating band. Added 12:50Z in the slot plan-8 left: move-prior, the learned movement prior (a model of how the strong bots move, fitted on 922 replay games; it predicts 50% of their moves in unseen games against 43% for a plain table, and on StuartSutcliffe's decisions lifts our movement agreement from 72.6% to 75.4%). Predicts: beats control, most against strong bots. Needs a release at or after 5636346. Added 13:35Z: learned, the movement prior together with the learned attack prior (models of when the strong bots fire, throw the frostburst and use the repulsor; frostburst timing predicted 89% of the time on unseen games, shots 76%). On StuartSutcliffe's decisions the pair lifts attack agreement from 49.3% to 82.6% and movement agreement to 74.6%. Predicts: at least as good as move-prior. Needs a release that has attack_prior_weight. Added 14:25Z: pad-fight. From today's replays of our own games against the top group (20 games, all lost): they take 1.75 power pads a game and we 0.40; in 9 of the 20 games they took a pad after we had stood at least four ticks within 3 tiles of it, no farther from it than they were, without a buff. A power pad is damage x3/2 for 50 ticks. The arm leaves for a pad in time, earns 15 for ending a turn on a power pad that is there, and gives a pad up only when the opponent is all but on it. Predicts: beats control against bots rated 2250 and up, with our power pads there rising from 0.4 toward 1 a game; no change against weaker bots, where we already get the pads. Needs a release that has pad_bonus (7dea220 or later). Added 14:45Z: tree. The new brain: with the opponent in view the turn comes from a tree search for both sides on the exact engine (victris_engine::mcts) run for 250 ms, with none of the hand-set terms of the policy. Offline, against the current search in the arena: 39% at 30 ms a move (18 games), 56% at 150 ms (18 games), 67% at 300 ms (30 games on fresh seeds). This arm is the ladder's confirmation of that offline result. It thinks about 250 ms on every tick with the opponent in view (server charge about 360 ms a tick), by design. Needs a release at or after the commit that adds tree_ms and forcing_depth. Added 15:40Z: tree-judged, which replaces tree. The tree search with a judgment of positions at its leaves, fitted on the search's own games (victris_engine::valuefeat, generation 1: 60 games of the plain search against itself), thinking 150 ms a move. Offline at 100 ms a move it beat the plain tree search 26-3-1 and the current search 23-7 over 30 games (the plain tree needed 300 ms for 20-10), and 32-14-2 at 60 ms. It leaves about 100 ms earlier than the tree arm, so a network burst costs it fewer turns. Predicts: beats control overall. Stop only on disqualification or a tree turn over 600 ms. Needs a release at or after the commit that adds tree_gen (which also keeps the tree off the gateway's quick fallback call). Changed 16:20Z on Mike's word: pad-fight and move-prior are retired (hand-written rule and a prior bolted onto the old bot; the search is the direction now), their records kept. Their slots go to the search: tree-judged, and tree-judged-300, the same search thinking 300 ms a move. Offline the search at 150 ms beat itself at 50 ms 22-3 with 5 draws over 30 games, so thinking time is the main lever; behind the gateway a late search answer costs only quality (the quick answer is played), and 300 ms a move keeps a 600-tick match at about 219 s of the 300 s budget. Predicts: tree-judged-300 beats tree-judged. Same stop rule: only on disqualification or a tree turn over 600 ms. Arms running after the change: control, tree-judged, tree-judged-300. Changed 17:40Z: tree-judged-300 is retired (17-13 at 30 games against tree-judged's 27-9; it loses more turns on slow connections, 65 against 26 by 17:30Z), records kept. Its slot goes to tree-dash-burst: tree-judged plus dash + repulsor in the search's move list for both sides. Studied tick by tick in the arena, the search did not foresee 45 of the 71 wall slams it took from today's bot, because a dash and the repulsor in the same tick slams from 4 to 5 tiles and that move was missing. With it, offline: 28-2 against today's bot (23-7 without; slam hp taken a game 18 against 26) and 20-9-1 against the search without it. Predicts: beats tree-judged. Needs a release at or after the commit that adds tree_dash_burst. Stop only on disqualification or a tree turn over 600 ms. Changed 18:05Z: tree-judged is retired (records kept); the flagship v8 (the same search on three threads) is the yardstick. Its slot goes to tree-fog: tree-dash-burst that also searches with the opponent out of sight, splitting its time over four guesses of where the opponent stands (drawn from the tiles the tracker says it could be on) and pooling the turns. Out of sight the old heuristic plays about half the turns; on the ladder since 16:41Z it took about 9 hp a game more than it dealt there. Offline: one guess lost 13-21-2; pooled guesses 13-9-2 (three threads) and 18-9-3 (four guesses on one thread) against the heuristic out of sight. Out of sight it thinks on every tick, so charge per turn rises to about the search's. Predicts: beats tree-dash-burst. Needs 8932110 or later. Stop only on disqualification or a tree turn over 600 ms. Changed 20:35Z: tree-fog is retired (53-41 against tree-dash-burst's 63-29 since 18:35Z; the flagship v9 with it 21-16; the flagship went to v10, the slam fix without fog). Its slot goes to tree-pads: tree-dash-burst with judgment row 6 (generation 1 plus 'nearer to a power pad', a pad there or back within 15 ticks, weighted 10 hp). From the replays of the search against bots rated 2400 and up: in our losses they took 1.7 power pads a game to our 0.8, and at tick 19, when the first pad appears, they stood 1.2 tiles from it and we 2.0. Offline the row takes more pads (2.2 against 1.5 a game) and is level with the search without it (15-13-2), so only the ladder against bots that fight for pads can tell. Predicts: more power pads against 2250 and up, and beats tree-dash-burst there. Needs the commit that adds rows 6 and 7 to VALUE_GENS. Stop only on our own disqualification or a think over 600 ms. Changed 22:25Z: tree-dash-burst is retired (76-38, 9 of 33 against 2400+; tree-pads 78-33, 14 of 31, and the flagship moved to tree-pads as v11 at 22:18Z). Its slot goes to tree-pads20: the same with the power pad race weighted 20 hp instead of 10 (judgment row 7). Asks whether more weight on the pad race helps further against the top bots. Runs on r38. Same stop rule. Changed 22:50Z: tree-pads20 is stopped at 13-17 (0 of 8 against 2500 and up) against tree-pads' 23-9 over the same games: 20 hp on the pad race is too much. Its slot goes to tree-pads-lead: tree-pads that also expects the opponent's standing shots to lead (aim at a tile we could step to) without leading its own. From the replays, the top twelve aim 7 to 15% of their shots one tile beside the opponent, and those shots were 7% of the damage we took in our losses to 2400 and up; the search could not expect them. Offline against the old bot it was level (24-6 either way); the old bot leads only some shots, so the ladder decides. Runs on r38. Same stop rule. Changed 23:45Z: tree-pads-lead is stopped (47-38 and 6 of 30 against 2400 and up, against tree-pads' 58-30 and 15 of 32 over the same games). Its slot goes to tree-pads-even40: tree-pads with 40% of each move list's prior spread evenly instead of 25%, so the search considers more of the opponent's less likely turns. In our losses to 2400 and up, 14% of the damage came from opponent turns the search gave under a tenth of the opponent's visits. Runs on r38. Same stop rule.
